newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek equities end sharply up on strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Greek equities end sharply up on strong demand.

text.p: The Greek bourse closed 3.26 percent higher on very heavy volume and analysts said the bourse's sharp rise was based on a positive market sentiment and strong demand for stocks.
"Investors are looking to buy equities and are in a rush to enter the bourse before prices rise even higher after their recent rally," said Constantinos Lygizos, an analyst at Egnatia Securities.
Market sentiment is very positive and Greek stocks keep on climbing on grounds of good economic forecasts, he said.
"Fresh money keeps flowing into the market. Also, February forecasted inflation at 6.5 percent seems achievable. Investors are expecting more good news of interest rate cuts as well," Lygizos added.
The market has discounted only good news so far and if bad news come out they could have an adverse effect on the market, he said.
Lygizos expected a correction soon and saw the next resistance levels at 1,460 and 1,490 points.
Prospects for this year's overall bourse performance are good, he said.
Shares of banks, certain industrial firms and construction companies will rise more on encouraging 1997 profit forecasts for 1997, he added.
Another analysts said the market rise was across-the-board.
"The rise has spread to medium and small capitalisation stocks," said George Kissandrakis, an analyst at Northern Greece Securities.
Kissandrakis expects a correction in the next few days and says the market would resist 1,450 points.
The Athens general share index ended 3.26 percent or 45.95 points higher at 1453.60 points from Tuesday's 1407.65, after opening at 1411.15.
Turnover was 44.8 billion drachmas on volume of 9.6 million shares. Advancers led decliners 162 to 71 with 25 issues unchanged on 258 issues traded.
